SHANGHAI TIMES. DEC 23 1938
Thorough Investigation
Of Child Slave Problem
Made By S.M.C. Official

Council Adopts Report And Recommendations Of
Chief Of Industrial Section; Full Details
Are Sent To The League Of Nations

ATTITUDE OF CHINESE COURTS TOWARD
SYSTEM HAS PRESENTED OBSTACLE

A comprehensive survey of the child slave problem, particularly as it affects girls and young women, has been made on behalf of the Shanghai Municipal Council and full details of this exhaustive study have been sent to the League of Nations.

On December 14 the Shanghai Municipal Council approved the minutes of the Watch Committee, which on December 7 had recommended the adoption of the report of the Chief of the Industrial Section, in her capacity as Protector of Mui Tsai, on the question of “Pei nu” (“Mui Tsai”) and related problems.

1.—The Shanghai Municipal Council should follow the concept developing elsewhere and decline to recognize any “pei nu” status or any status in any way suggestive of servility.
This implies that there should be no separate register of “pei nu.”
2.—The Council should again follow the emphasis elsewhere developing and express its rence of responsibility for transferred children and adolescents by seeking by all available means to have such reported to Council Officials concerned, and by offering protection to them.
To implement these principles the Council adopted the following recommendations:—
1.—The Shanghai Municipal Council should seek by all available means the reporting of transferred children and adolescents to the Council officials concerned.
2.—There should be set up a small Child Protection Section. The present title of “Protector of Mui Tsai” which the Chief of the Industrial Section concurrently holds should be changed to “Chief, Child Protection Section.”
3.—The existing Chinese social worker should be confirmed in her appointment as assistant and she should be considered the nucleus of a small group of Chinese women assistants acting as supervisors under the Chief of the Child Protection Section.
4.—There should be close collaboration with Chinese and foreign organizations in the field of child protection.

By decision of the Council the full report will be forwarded to the League of Nations, while an abridged form is published in the “Municipal Gazette” of December 23.

Detailed Information
The report covers detailed information concerning 37 cases of “pei nu” or “mui tsai” who have come to the attention of the Municipal Police during the last 10 months. It draws attention to the 131 cases of abduction, rape, assault into prostitution and abandonment.

The report further covers a study of 176 cases of girls either formerly or at present “pei nu”; 72 girls who have been sold or mortgaged into a life of prostitution; and of 27 girls bound by contract to a period of service in industrial undertakings where their earnings are the property of a contractor. These studies are published in full in appendices to the full report. It examines the attitudes of Chinese Courts toward the question of money in a transaction involving transfer of children and adolescents on the basis of a test case taken into the First Special District Court in 1937. The conclusion can be drawn that “The decisions of the Chinese Courts are not clear as to what constitutes slavery. What they state is that before a conviction can be obtained, it must be proved that a person alleged to be a slave is treated as a slave and deprived of his or her right of self-control. The general policy of the Courts seems to be that the buying and selling of children is not illegal provided that the child is bought for the purpose of adoption.” In none of the cases studied where any claim for adoption was put forward had there been any legal adoption in accordance with the Chinese Civil Code.

Studied Abroad
What should be the Council’s Administrative Policy?:
The report deduces the fact that it is evident that there is a wider custom of transfer of girls into the control of others than is exemplified in the “pei nu” group. This view, it is stated, coincides with the conception expressed to the League of Nations Slavery Committee from other sources. The Chinese Government, the British Government, and the Malayan Government have each expressed their views that the question of “pei nu” is part of the larger problem of child protection. Malaya has recently accepted in principle recommendations which will entail repeal of existing “mui tsai” legislation, replacing it by general child protection measures. During the absence on long leave of the Chief of the Industrial Section calls were paid in Geneva on permanent officials of the League of Nations concerned with the problem, and in London and Ottawa members of League Committees dealing with “mui tsai” and related questions. 工部局官员对童奴问题进行彻底调查

市议会通过工业股股长的报告及建议；详细情况已报送国际联盟

中国法院对该制度的态度构成障碍

代表上海公共租界工部局对童奴问题，特别是涉及女孩和年轻女性的问题，进行了一次全面调查，这项详尽研究的全部细节已送交国际联盟。

12月14日，上海公共租界工部局批准了警务委员会的会议记录，该委员会曾于12月7日建议采纳工业股股长以“妹仔保护官”身份提交的关于“婢女”（“妹仔”）及相关问题的报告。

在通过该报告时，[原文此处语句不通，似有缺漏，大意可能为：此类案件数量远少于其他类型的剥削女孩案件]。

报告中列出的要点如下：—
1.—上海公共租界工部局应遵循其他地方正在发展的理念，拒绝承认任何“婢女”身份或任何暗示奴役性质的身份。
这意味着不应设立单独的“婢女”登记册。
2.—工部局应再次遵循其他地方日益强调的做法，表明其对被转手儿童和青少年的责任，即通过各种可用手段促使向工部局有关官员报告此类情况，并向他们提供保护。
为实施这些原则，工部局通过了以下建议：—
1.—上海公共租界工部局应通过各种可用手段，促使向工部局有关官员报告被转手的儿童和青少年。
2.—应设立一个小型的儿童保护股。工业股股长目前兼任的“妹仔保护官”头衔应改为“儿童保护股股长”。
3.—现任中国籍社会工作者应确认为助理，并应将其视为一小群中国籍女性助理的核心，这些助理在儿童保护股股长的领导下担任督导员。
4.—应与从事儿童保护领域的中外组织密切合作。

根据工部局的决定，完整报告将送交国际联盟，而删节版则刊登在12月23日的《市政公报》上。

详细信息
该报告涵盖了在过去10个月中引起工部局警务处注意的37起“婢女”或“妹仔”案件的详细信息。报告提请注意131起绑架、强奸、强迫卖淫和遗弃案件。

报告还涵盖了对176名曾经或目前是“婢女”的女孩的研究；72名被卖或抵押进入卖淫生活的女孩；以及27名通过契约绑定在工业企业服役一段时间的女孩，她们的收入归包工头所有。这些研究全文刊登在完整报告的附录中。报告基于1937年提交至第一特区地方法院的一个测试案例，审视了中国法院在涉及儿童和青少年转手的交易中对金钱问题的态度。可以得出的结论是：“中国法院对于什么构成奴隶制的判决并不明确。他们指出，要在定罪前，必须证明被指称为奴隶的人受到像奴隶般的对待，并被剥夺了其自我控制权。法院的一般政策似乎是，只要购买儿童是为了收养目的，买卖儿童并不违法。”在所研究的案件中，凡提出收养主张的，均没有按照《中华民国民法典》进行过合法收养。

海外研究
工部局应采取何种行政政策？：
报告推断出一个事实，即显然存在比“婢女”群体所体现的更广泛的女孩转由他人控制的习惯。据称，这一观点与国际联盟奴隶制委员会从其他来源表达的概念一致。中国政府、英国政府和马来亚政府各自表示，“婢女”问题是儿童保护更大问题的一部分。马来亚最近原则上接受了各项建议，这将导致废除现行的“妹仔”立法，代之以一般的儿童保护措施。在工业股股长长期休假期间，她在日内瓦拜访了国际联盟负责该问题的常任官员，并在伦敦和渥太华拜访了处理“妹仔”及相关问题的国际联盟委员会成员。此外，她还得以查阅有关各国政府在转手儿童问题上的政策的报告和

其他地区
报告考察了香港、马来亚、锡兰和印度海得拉巴土邦的情况。在后一个邦，广义上的这一问题得到了处理，国际联盟奴隶制委员会副主席乔治·麦克斯韦尔爵士（Sir George Maxwell）在就此撰写文章时指出：—
“关键在于认识到这样一个事实：当极度贫困迫使父母摆脱他们的孩子时，切实且人道的做法是确保被转手儿童的福祉……在香港和马来亚，‘妹仔’立法的失败是由于官方忽视了一个基本事实，即社会和经济习俗不能仅靠禁令来根除。”
报告接着指出，中国政府1936年1月的法规要求释放被拘禁的女孩，但不要求将其作为一个特殊类别进行登记。“各地日益认识到，不应存在一个被称为‘婢女’的单独且隐含奴役性质的群体，因此不应有‘婢女’登记册。重点在于当局应关注任何被转手的儿童和青少年，无论其转手目的为何，也无论是暂时还是半永久性地置于他人控制之下。”
报告承认，如果现实地看待各种可能性，这种包容性的方法使得难以制定关于国际租界行政行动的建议。尽管如此，仍应努力促使当局收到关于被转手女孩的报告。上海在其他一些行政处理问题的例子中，由于工部局无权强制，因此缺乏强制力支持。这些部分措施即使不完全成功，也是有益的。工部局要求的阐明往往倾向于在其他方向上得到执行。
因此，人们相信，在报告被转手女孩方面可以迈出第一步。由于工部局职员中有一名社会工作者，许多需要保护的女孩案件已向她报告，其中往往来自意想不到的来源。随着正式且反复地阐明工部局的政策和要求，利用宣传方法，并与从事儿童保护领域的中外组织密切合作，肯定会有大量案件被报告。这样就迈出了行政起步阶段，以便如果将来能基于国家立法实施强制措施，则已取得一些进展，同时在此期间，许多女孩将获得帮助过上更幸福的生活，并从堕落生活中获救。

SHANGHAI TIMES, DEC 23 1938
CHILD PROTECTION
That we should learn from experience is one of the most favoured of precepts. though so often seen to be ignored. But a case wherein profit has been gained from the experiences of others is furnished by the carefully-drawn-up report of the Chief of the Industrial Section of the S.M.C. in her capacity of Protector of Mui Tsai, a digest of which appears in this issue and a longer, though abridged, form in to-day's Municipal Gazette. The important point upon which wisdom has been learned is in the rejection of the idea that mui tsai, or per nu, as young "transferred" domestic girls are called here, should be officially registered or given any status in any way suggestive of servility. When the problem of mui tsai was first brought to public notice in Hongkong some years ago, through the efforts of a retired British naval officer and his wife, the existence of so-called "slave girls" created such an outcry in London and elsewhere that the Hongkong Government, against all the advice of the Colony's leading Chinese residents, was more or less forced to pass a Mui Tsai Ordinance which called for the registration of all young girls in domestic service to whose parents or guardians there had been something in the way of payment made for their transfer. Notwithstanding the fact that evasion of the law became widespread owing to a form of adoption being resorted to, there was a good deal of registration carried out as regards the girls actually in service at the time, but the stigma of being a registered mui tsai was of considerable, and unfortunate, effect. By the Ordinance, which was several times amended, it was made a crime to take into domestic service any new mui tsai, the idea being that, by such a prohibition, the passing of a few years would see the end of the system. It has done nothing of the kind, for adoption and other ruses have defeated the legislature's intention in that regard and has done much to nullify the application of that care and protection which was the primary purpose to be served. It is worth repeating here the sentiment of Sir George Maxwell, Vice-Chairman of the League of Nation's Slavery Committee: "The keynote is the recognition of the fact that when dire poverty compels parents to get rid of their children, the practical and humane method is to ensure the well-being of the transferred children. . . . In Hong-kong and Malaya the failure of mui tsai legislation is due to official blindness to the elementary fact that a social and economic custom is not eradicated by prohibition." Horror at the word "slavery" effects nothing worthwhile unless it results in benefit to the "slave" and it is the first duty of the authorities to see that there should be no creation of a servile group but rather the extension of whatever care and protection can be afforded not only to servant girls but to all women and children who are made the chattels of traffickers for any purpose whatsoever.
As that is the keynote of Miss Hinder's report it can be given hearty welcome and should evoke a great deal of co-operative response on the part of all Chinese and foreign organisations working in the field of child protection. The Council has very wisely approved of the principle that it should have a sense of responsibility for transferred children and adolescents by seeking by all available means to have such reported to the Council officials concerned, and by offering protection to them. A small Child Protection Section is to be set up, and the present title of "Protector of Mui Tsai" which the Chief of the Industrial Section concurrently holds is to be changed to that of "Chief, Child Protection Section." It is a much better title and more clearly represents the function of the office. The existing Chinese social worker in the employ of the Council, Miss Chi Chih-ting, is to be confirmed in her appointment as assistant, and she is to be considered as the nucleus of a small group of Chinese women assistants acting as supervisors under the Chief. With this "machinery" and with what is hoped will be close collaboration between and with, Chinese and foreign organizations, there will be an active body of workers concerned wholly with the fate and misfortunes of those girls and young women who are now exploited by the callous and unscrupulous. Few people need much enlightenment on the extent of the sordid exploitation which goes on in this city to-day and although social workers cannot hope to clean up a situation which is chronic and of considerable magnitude they can come to the rescue of those who are either unwilling victims or suffering physical and mental hardships. One welcomes the recognition which the report makes that institutional care does not constitute the best arrangement that can be made for children needing the protection of the authorities and it is encouraging to read that a study of new approaches is to be made when conditions shall have become more normal. As a matter of fact, in present circumstances, service in "honest" homes is a happy lot compared with many, and any edict against mui tsai, even if that were possible, would work considerable hardship. It is not an offence against Chinese law to keep a mui tsai, but the concern of the authorities must be to see that no girl is ill-treated or forced into a life of immorality. There is no space here to cover all the ground which the report brings within its purview, but a careful reading of it is recommended not only for its educational value on a problem upon which enlightened public opinion is essential but for the encouragement of that co-operation upon which the authorities have largely to depend. Basically, of course, this problem of mui tsai, alleged "adoption," of dancing girls, "girl guides," prostitution, and other forms of the social evil resides mainly in the low economic status of the Chinese masses and the over-production of children. It is wholly unnatural for parents to desire to part with their children, or to see them living degraded lives, and the Chinese are no exception to that universal instinct. But poverty drives, while the avaricious and unscrupulous seek to profit. It is nothing less than China's social problem which is involved.

《上海泰晤士报》，1938年12月23日

保护儿童

从经验中吸取教训是最受推崇的格言之一，尽管人们经常看到它被忽视。但是，工部局工业科科长在兼任妹仔保护官一职时精心撰写的报告，提供了一个从他人经验中获益的案例；该报告的摘要刊登在本期报纸上，较长但经删节的版本则刊登在今日的《市政公报》上。从中汲取智慧的重要一点在于，摒弃了将妹仔（即此处所称的年轻“转让”女佣，或称“婢女”）进行官方登记或赋予任何暗示奴役地位的想法。几年前，通过一位退休英国海军军官及其夫人的努力，妹仔问题首次在香港引起公众关注，所谓“奴隶少女”的存在在伦敦及其他地方引发了如此强烈的抗议，以至于香港政府不顾该殖民地主要中国居民的所有建议，或多或少被迫通过了一项《妹仔条例》，要求对所有在其父母或监护人因转让而获得某种形式付款的情况下从事家务劳动的年轻女孩进行登记。尽管由于采取了一种收养形式来规避法律，导致逃避法律的现象普遍存在，但在当时实际服役的女孩中仍有不少进行了登记，然而，被登记为妹仔的污名产生了相当大且不幸的影响。根据该经过多次修订的条例，接纳任何新的妹仔进入家庭服务构成犯罪，其设想是，通过这种禁令，几年之后该制度便会终结。但事实并非如此，收养和其他诡计挫败了立法者在这方面的意图，并在很大程度上使原本旨在提供的关怀和保护落空。在此值得重申国际联盟奴隶制委员会副主席乔治·麦克斯韦尔爵士（Sir George Maxwell）的观点：“关键在于承认这样一个事实：当极度贫困迫使父母送走子女时，切实且人道的方法是确保被转让儿童的福祉……在香港和马来亚，妹仔立法的失败是由于官方忽视了这样一个基本事实：社会和经济习俗不能靠禁令来根除。”除非能转化为对“奴隶”的实际利益，否则对“奴隶”一词的恐惧不会产生任何有价值的结果；当局的首要职责是确保不形成一个奴役群体，而是尽可能扩展关怀和保护，不仅给予女佣，也给予所有沦为人口贩子商品的女性及儿童，无论其目的为何。

既然这是欣德小姐（Miss Hinder）报告的主旨，那么该报告理应受到热烈欢迎，并应激起所有从事儿童保护工作的中外团体的广泛合作响应。工部局非常明智地批准了这样一项原则：即工部局应对被转让的儿童和青少年负有责任感，为此要利用一切可用手段促使向工部局有关官员申报此类情况，并向他们提供保护。将设立一个小型的儿童保护科，目前由工业科科长兼任的“妹仔保护官”头衔将改为“儿童保护科科长”。这是一个更好的头衔，更清晰地代表了该职位的职能。工部局聘用的现有中国社会工作者纪志定（Chi Chih-ting，音译）小姐将被正式任命为助理，她将被视为一个小型中国女性助理团队的核心，这些助理将在科长领导下担任督导员。有了这套“机制”，并希望在中外组织之间及与它们建立密切合作，就将拥有一支积极的工作队伍，全心全意关注那些目前正被冷酷无情和不择手段者剥削的女孩和年轻女性的命运与不幸。对于当今这座城市中发生的肮脏剥削的程度，很少有人需要多加启蒙；虽然社会工作者无法指望彻底清理这种长期存在且规模相当大的局面，但他们可以救助那些要么是不情愿的受害者、要么遭受身心磨难的人。人们欢迎该报告所确认的一点，即机构照护并不构成需要当局保护的儿童的最佳安排方案；令人鼓舞的是，报告指出，待局势更加正常后，将对新的方法进行调研。事实上，在目前的情况下，与许多其他处境相比，在“正派”家庭中服役已算是幸运的结局；即使有可能，任何禁止妹仔的法令也会造成相当大的困难。蓄养妹仔并不违反中国法律，但当局必须关注的是确保没有女孩受到虐待或被迫过上不道德的生活。此处没有篇幅涵盖报告所涉及的全部内容，但建议仔细阅读该报告，这不仅因为它对一个需要开明公众舆论的问题具有教育价值，还因为它有助于鼓励当局在很大程度上所依赖的合作。从根本上说，当然，妹仔、所谓的“收养”、舞女、“女向导”、卖淫以及其他形式的社会罪恶问题，主要在于中国大众的低经济地位和儿童过剩。父母希望与子女分离，或看着他们过着堕落的生活，这完全是违背天性的，中国人也不例外于这种普遍的本能。但是贫困驱使人们这样做，而贪婪和无良之徒则试图从中牟利。这无非是涉及中国的社会问题。

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, MAY 20, 1936

Slave Fines
Are Declared
Too Small

W.C.T.U. Official Urges
Stern Measures To
Curb Evil

20,000 SLAVES IN
GREATER SHANGHAI

Mrs. Herman Liu Says
Majority Live In 2
Foreign Areas

By WOO KYATANG

The punishment for keeping un-registered slaves as provided by the law promulgated by the National Government was deemed too lenient by Mrs. Herman C. E. Liu, General Secretary of the W.C.T.U. of China, in an interview with THE CHINA PRESS yesterday.

Mrs. Liu's statement represented the consensus of other people, engaged actively in emancipation work here, who were approached by the reporter.

The article to which Mrs. Liu referred called for fines of below $10 for anyone found keeping unregistered slaves after June 30.

"This fine is too small," Mrs. Liu said. "If this campaign sponsored by the Government is really to be successful, the punishment should be at least fines over $100 coupled with prison sentences."

In making the statement, Mrs. Liu pointed out that she realized that the slavery question is a deep-rooted one in China. Because of this fact, she felt that a more direct measure is needed to drive the slave-keeping custom completely out of Chinese society.

20,000 Slaves In City

Questioned regarding the estimated number of slaves known to be kept in Shanghai families, both Mrs. Liu and other emancipation officials hesitated to give a definite figure. Due to the lack of reliable data, the nearest estimate shows that there are at least 20,000 slaves in three areas in Shanghai. Mrs. Liu was inclined to believe that a majority of this number is to be found within the Settlement and the French Concession.

"Only the wealthy or the near-wealthy have slaves, and most of the well-to-do families in Shanghai are concentrated in the foreign-controlled areas," she said.

The co-operation of Settlement and Concession authorities, with the Chinese officials in this nation-wide slave-suppression campaign is absolutely necessary, Mrs. Liu averred.

No Co-operation To Date

So far, she said, there has been no definite understanding on this question between the Municipality of Greater Shanghai and the officials of the foreign-administered areas.

In the office of the National Child Welfare Association, which is also working on the slavery problem, the reporter was told that the actual progress for slave registration has been extremely slow.

Records show that during March, the month the registration period got under way, and to the end of April, only 30 families came voluntarily to the Bureau of Public Safety to register their slaves. A slight increase was noted in May when another 30 were recorded.

June 30 Deadline

All the slaves in Shanghai, whatever their actual number, are due to be registered by June 30. After that date, any family found keeping slaves without the proper registration will be subject to fines.

Officials of the Child Welfare Association found slow progress is due to a combination of factors, including ignorance on the part of the young slaves, and the dogged unwillingness on the part of the owners to forsake their human chattel.

The Association employs several investigators who make inquiries based on reports, often anonymous, received at the Child Welfare headquarters.

Acting on this sort of information, the Association officials will visit the homes. This visit usually is the initial step in a long and controversial fight for rescuing the slaves.

Use Same Excuse

The owners will always tell the investigators that the little girl or the little boy in their household is a relative whose parents have died. The regular line of defense of the owners when cornered by the Association officials runs something like this: "This is a family affair. It's none of your business. The girl (or boy) is merely boarding here. If she (or he) eats, it's natural that we would ask her to do a bit of work once in a while."

The Association officials found that with this kind of defense, it is often hard to pin anything on the slave owners.

Typical Case Cited

A concrete example of their case work was given to the reporter to illustrate the case.

Several weeks ago a report was received by the Welfare Association saying that a woman named Mrs. Chu Chen-see, living at an address at Pao An Road, Chapei, was ill-treating a slave girl. An investigator sent to the address found a 13-year-old girl, named Chu Hsiu-lien, in ragged clothing doing heavy house work.

Mrs. Chu, when questioned said that the girl was adopted by her when the latter was three years old. "She is not a slave, but my adopted daughter," the woman insisted.

When Hsiu-lien was sent to the Lester Chinese Hospital, several marks showing she had been beaten were found on her body. Also neighbors of Mrs. Chu testified that they often saw Hsiu-lien lashed by Mrs. Chu. A suit was finally brought against the woman. The judgment of the case awarded Hsiu-lien to the care of the Child Welfare Association.

《字林西报》，1936年5月20日，星期三

奴役罚款
被指
过低

妇禁会官员呼吁
采取严厉措施
以遏制此恶习

大上海地区有
两万奴婢

刘赫曼夫人称
大多数生活在
两个外国辖区

作者：WOO KYATANG

中国妇女基督教禁酒联盟（W.C.T.U.）总干事刘赫曼（Herman C. E. Liu）夫人在昨日接受《字林西报》采访时认为，国民政府颁布的法律中关于蓄养未登记奴婢的处罚规定过于宽纵。

刘夫人的陈述代表了记者所接触到的其他在此间积极从事解放工作的人士的共识。

刘夫人所指的文章称，凡在6月30日后被发现蓄养未登记奴婢者，将被处以10美元以下的罚款。

“这笔罚款太少了，”刘夫人说。“如果政府发起的这场运动真的要取得成功，惩罚至少应是100美元以上的罚款并辅以监禁。”

在发表上述声明时，刘夫人指出，她意识到奴役问题在中国根深蒂固。鉴于这一事实，她认为需要采取更直接的措施，将蓄奴习俗彻底从中国社会中驱除。

市内有两万奴婢

当被问及已知上海家庭中蓄养的奴婢估计人数时，刘夫人和其他解放事务官员均不愿给出确切数字。由于缺乏可靠数据，最接近的估算显示，上海三个区域内至少有20,000名奴婢。刘夫人倾向于相信，其中大多数人位于公共租界和法租界内。

她说：“只有富人或近富阶层才拥有奴婢，而上海大多数富裕家庭都集中在外国人控制的区域。”

刘夫人断言，在这场全国性的禁奴运动中，租界和公董局当局与中国官员的合作绝对必要。

迄今尚无合作

她说，迄今为止，大上海市政府与外国管理区域的官员之间在此问题上尚未达成明确的谅解。

在同样致力于解决奴役问题的全国儿童福利协会办公室，记者获悉，奴婢登记的实际进展极其缓慢。

记录显示，在登记期开始的3月份以及直到4月底，仅有30个家庭自愿前往公安局登记其奴婢。5月份略有增加，又记录了30例。

6月30日为截止日期

无论实际数量如何，上海所有的奴婢都须在6月30日前完成登记。在此日期之后，任何被发现蓄养奴婢而未进行适当登记的家庭将面临罚款。

儿童福利协会的官员发现，进展缓慢是由多种因素造成的，包括年轻奴婢自身的无知，以及主人顽固地不愿放弃其人身财产。

该协会雇佣了几名调查员，根据在儿童福利总部收到的报告（通常是匿名的）进行调查。

根据此类信息，协会官员将上门走访。这种走访通常是漫长且充满争议的解救奴婢斗争的第一步。

使用同样的借口

主人总是告诉调查员，他们家中的小女孩或小男孩是亲戚，其父母已故。当被协会官员逼问时，主人的常规辩护辞令大致如下：“这是家事。与你们无关。这个女孩（或男孩）只是在这里寄宿。如果她（或他）吃饭，我们偶尔让她做点活也是自然的。”

协会官员发现，面对这种辩护，往往很难坐实奴隶主的罪名。

引用典型案例

向记者提供了一个具体的案例工作实例以作说明。

几周前，福利协会收到一份报告，称住在闸北宝安路某址的一名朱陈氏（Chu Chen-see，音译）妇女虐待一名婢女。派往该地址的调查员发现一名名叫朱秀莲（Chu Hsiu-lien，音译）的13岁女孩，衣衫褴褛，做着繁重的家务。

朱氏在接受询问时表示，该女孩在三岁时被她收养。“她不是奴婢，而是我的养女，”该妇女坚持道。

当秀莲被送往莱斯德华人医院（Lester Chinese Hospital）时，在她身上发现了多处表明曾遭殴打的痕迹。此外，朱氏的邻居作证说，他们经常看到秀莲被朱氏鞭打。最终对该妇女提起诉讼。案件判决将秀莲交由儿童福利协会监护。

据昨日《新闻报》刊登的一篇报道，当地中国政府和民间团体已制定组织婢女解放委员会的计划。

除了组织该委员会的计划外，全国儿童福利协会和妇女基督教禁酒联盟在与公安局协商后，也共同制定了建立女仆培训学院的计划。

建立女仆培训学院的准备工作目前由上海本地女性领袖、沪江大学校长夫人刘赫曼（Herman C. E. Liu）夫人负责。

Labour

Local Silk Filatures - Situation

During the month of February, two out of the four
silk filatures in the Settlement have been operating with
a total complement of 900 hands. Of the fifty-one filatures
in Chinese controlled territory, only eleven have been
operating with a total complement of 5,190 hands.

Foh Sing Cigarette Factory - Situation

The workers of the Foh Sing Cigarette Factory,
521 Macao Road, resumed operations at 1 p.m. February 28
in accordance with the terms for the settlement of the
strike reached on February 27. The situation in the
factory this morning is normal.

Miscellaneous

Prohibition of female slavery - Order of the
Executive Yuan

Copies of a proclamation issued by the Bureau of
Public Safety, announcing the order of the Executive Yuan
of the National Government prohibiting female slavery,
were posted on February 27 in Chinese controlled territory.
This order states that to enforce the prohibition, female
slaves will be registered by the Bureau of Public Safety
with effect from March 1, 1936 and the proclamation urges
the slaves, their masters, or representatives to carry out
the registration order within the period from March 1, 1936

February 5, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE REGISTRATION OF SLAVE GIRLS.

Acting on instructions from the Shanghai City Government, the Bureau of Public Safety is making preparations for the registration of slave girls. The matter is one of great importance, because it seriously affects the emancipation of poor and destitute girls, and also affects the national prestige and moral laws. Therefore, the Bureau of Public Safety has instructed Ying Kwo Tsz (殷國之), Officer-in-charge of the Relief Department, to expedite the work.

In an interview with a reporter of this paper, Ying Kwo Tsz stated that the Commissioner of the Bureau of Public Safety is taking the matter up very seriously. Registration will commence on March 1.

A census of slave girls will be taken and their names will be registered. The period of investigation will last four months, and will be extended by two months if necessary.

The following measures will be observed :-
(1) During the period of investigation, persons who have slave girls should report to the Bureau for registration or ask someone to do so on their behalf.
(2) Registered slave girls will be unconditionally emancipated and set free. Minors, homeless girls or those from poor families which cannot afford to support them, will be sent to the Relief Home or other benevolent institutions.
(3) Girls over 16 years of age, who are homeless; will be selected husbands on their behalf, provided they give their consent.
(4) Emancipated girls, who are homeless or the addresses of whose relations are unknown, will be taken care of by a person appointed by the Relief Home or some other benevolent institution.
(5) Persons who keep slave girls after the expiry of the appointed period and do not report for registration, will be fined $10.00 or less and will be required to register.
(6) The fines will be used to defray the expenses of the Relief Home or other benevolent institutions of this city.
(7) Persons who do not liberate their slave girls will be sent to the judicial organs for punishment according to law.
(8) Emancipated girls above 16 years of age may be employed as female servants if they so desire. The wages will be according to the cost of living in Shanghai.

Central China Daily News :-

THE TOMB TO THE UNKNOWN HERO.

Leaders of various Chinese circles in this locality recently raised funds for the construction of a tomb to the Unknown Hero at Miao Hong Tsung, Kiangwan, in memory of the soldiers and civilians who fell during the January 28 Incident. The tomb was completed in December last year.
The unveiling ceremony will take place at 10 a.m. February 16.

《申报》及其他本地报纸：-

婢女登记。

根据上海市政府的指示，公安局正在准备进行婢女登记。此事至关重要，因为它严重影响贫困孤苦女孩的解放，同时也影响国家声誉和道德法规。因此，公安局已指示救济科主管殷國之加快此项工作。

殷國之在接受本报记者采访时称，公安局局长非常重视此事。登记将于3月1日开始。

将对婢女进行普查并登记姓名。调查期为四个月，如有必要可延长两个月。

将采取以下措施：-
(1) 在调查期间，拥有婢女的人应向公安局报告以进行登记，或委托他人代为办理。
(2) 已登记的婢女将无条件获得解放和自由。未成年人、无家可归的女孩或来自无力抚养她们的贫困家庭的女孩，将被送往救济院或其他慈善机构。
(3) 对于16岁以上无家可归的女孩，将在征得其同意的情况下，为她们挑选丈夫。
(4) 对于无家可归或其亲属地址不明的被解放女孩，将由救济院或其他慈善机构指定的人员照顾。
(5) 在指定期限届满后仍蓄养婢女且不报告登记者，将被处以10.00美元或以下的罚款，并被要求登记。
(6) 罚款将用于支付本市救济院或其他慈善机构的费用。
(7) 不释放其婢女的人将被移送司法机关依法惩处。
(8) 16岁以上的被解放女孩如愿意，可受雇为女仆。工资将根据上海的生活成本确定。

January 28, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

Shun Pao publishes the following telegram from Nanking :-

REGULATIONS PROHIBITING THE KEEPING OF SLAVE GIRLS.

On January 22, the Ministry of Interior promulgated, with the approval of the Executive Yuan, the following set of regulations prohibiting the keeping of slave girls :-
Article 1. - The keeping of slave girls in the name of charity or as adopted daughters is prohibited by these Regulations.
Article 2. - The official organs authorized to enforce the present Regulations shall be the Metropolitan Constabulary of Nanking and the Bureaux of Public Safety of municipalities and provinces.
Article 3. - As soon as they receive the present Regulations, the authorities of various official organs charged with the enforcement of the Regulations shall issue a public notice during the period of investigation and shall instruct their subordinates to ascertain the number of slave girls in their jurisdiction.
Article 4. - Owners of slave girls should apply to the proper authorities for registration of the slave girls during the period of investigation. Slave girls may also apply for registration or ask some persons to do so for them.
Article 5. - Freedom is unconditionally restored to slave girls once they have been properly registered. They may be sent to benevolent institutions if they are under age and homeless or if their families are financially unable to support them.
Article 6. - Official organs charged with the enforcement of the present Regulations may, with the girls' consent, arrange marriages for those freed slave girls who are homeless and who are above the age of 16.
Article 7. - Slave girls who have attained full age are allowed to enter the service of their former owners as maid-servants. The question of their wages shall be fixed by the official organs according to the cost of living of the district. In case of minors who are homeless or the addresses of whose families are unknown, the official organs may appoint local benevolent institutions as their guardians.
Article 8. - Owners of slave girls who fail to apply for registration at the expiry of the period of investigation as stipulated in Article 3 of the present Regulations are liable to a fine of not more than $20 by the official organs, in addition to which they shall be ordered to register their slave girls.
Article 9. - Whoever refuses to give freedom to their registered slave girls shall be sent to judicial organs to be dealt with.
Article 10. - Every month official organs enforcing these Regulations shall fill in the registration forms of slave girls and forward same to the Ministry of Interior.
Article 11. - The present Regulations nullify all measures previously promulgated governing the prohibition of keeping slaves and slave girls.
Article 12. - The present Regulations shall come into force on the date of their promulgation.

禁止蓄养婢女规章。

1月22日，内政部经行政院批准，公布了以下禁止蓄养婢女的规章：
第一条。- 本规章禁止以慈善或收养义女的名义蓄养婢女。
第二条。- 负责执行本规章的官方机构应为南京首都警察厅及各市、省公安局。
第三条。- 各负责执行本规章的官方机构当局在收到本规章后，应在调查期间发布公告，并指示其下属查明辖区内的婢女数量。
第四条。- 婢女主人应在调查期间向有关当局申请婢女登记。婢女也可自行申请登记或委托他人代为申请。
第五条。- 婢女一经正式登记，即无条件恢复自由。若其未成年且无家可归，或其家庭无力抚养，可将其送往慈善机构。
第六条。- 负责执行本规章的官方机构可在征得女孩同意的情况下，为那些无家可归且年满16岁的获释婢女安排婚姻。
第七条。- 已成年的婢女允许受雇于原主人为女仆。其工资数额由官方机构根据当地生活费用确定。对于无家可归的未成年人或家庭住址不明者，官方机构可指定当地慈善机构为其监护人。
第八条。- 未在本规章第三条规定的调查期届满时申请登记的婢女主人，将由官方机构处以不超过20元的罚款，并被责令登记其婢女。
第九条。- 拒绝给予已登记婢女自由者，将移送司法机关处理。
第十条。- 执行本规章的官方机构每月应填写婢女登记表，并报送内政部。
第十一条。- 本规章废止此前公布的关于禁止蓄养奴婢和婢女的所有措施。
第十二条。- 本规章自公布之日起施行。

October 24, 1932.
Afternoon Translation.

MISCELLANEOUS.

Sin Wan Pao:

BAN ON PRACTICE OF KEEPING SLAVES AND SLAVE GIRLS FOR
SALE OR PURCHASE.

The following regulations governing the
prohibition of the practice of keeping slaves and slave
girls which were recently sanctioned by the Executive
Yuan have been promulgated by the Bureau of Public
Safety and the Bureau of Social Affairs in the Sin Wan
Pao:-
1. The keeping of slaves and slave girls for purpose of
sale, purchase or donation and not for purpose of
employment is to be prohibited.
2. The following process will be adopted in enforcing
this prohibition:-
(a) To give advice, (b) To effect the release of
victims, (d) To afford them relief, (e) To impose
punishment.
3. Those organs under the direct control of District
Municipal and Hsien Government, or of Provincial
Governments should assist the Police authorities in
conducting a thorough investigation into the practice
of keeping slaves and slave girls and all persons
discovered keeping slaves are first to be advised not
to keep them any more. This advice is to be
forwarded by the Bureau of Public Safety.
4. After receiving this advice, the persons concerned
should release the slaves within a certain specified
period and should they desire the slaves to work as
servants, they should employ them and pay them wages but
both parties will have the freedom to sever relations
at any time.
5. If the number of slaves released is too large and the
employment system can not be applied to them, the
following relief measures are to be adopted:-
(a) Slaves who have not yet reached their majority,
are to be sent back to their families. If they
have no families or if their families do not
want to receive them, they are to be sent to the
Relief Institution of the district, and if there is
no such institution, they are to be sent by the
district government to any benevolent institution.
(b) Adult slaves are to be permitted to marry and to
seek employment. If they cannot find a wife or
employment, they are to be sent to benevolent
institutes by the District Government.
6. Persons who ignore this prohibition and continue to
keep slaves at the expiration of the specified period
or by keeping new slaves after the promulgation of
this prohibition are to be fined $300 or less and
their slaves are to be compulsorily released.
7. All District and Hsien Governments and Bureaux of
Public Safety should make a report to the Provincial
Government on the results of prohibition within three
months and these reports are to be forwarded by the
Provincial Government to the Ministry of Home Affairs
for consideration.
8. The above measures come into force from the date of
promulgation.

《新闻报》：

禁止买卖奴婢及婢女习俗。

以下关于禁止蓄养奴婢及婢女习俗的规章，近日获行政院核准，已由公安局和社会局在《新闻报》上公布：
1. 禁止以出售、购买或捐赠为目的，而非以雇佣为目的蓄养奴婢及婢女。
2. 执行此禁令将采取以下程序：(a) 劝告，(b) 实施受害者释放，(d) 提供救济，(e) 实施惩罚。
3. 直属于区市政府、县政府或省政府管辖的各机关应协助警察当局对蓄养奴婢及婢女的习俗进行彻底调查，所有被发现蓄养奴婢的人首先应被劝告不再蓄养。此劝告由公安局发出。
4. 有关人员在收到此劝告后，应在指定的期限内释放奴婢；若希望奴婢作为仆人工作，应雇佣他们并支付工资，但双方均有权随时解除关系。
5. 若释放的奴婢数量过多，无法适用雇佣制度，则应采取以下救济措施：
(a) 尚未成年的奴婢，应送返其家庭。若无家庭或其家庭不愿接收，应送往该区救济院；若无此类机构，则由区政府送往任何慈善机构。
(b) 成年奴婢应被允许结婚和求职。若找不到配偶或工作，由区政府送往慈善机构。
6. 无视此禁令，在指定期限届满后仍继续蓄养奴婢，或在此禁令公布后蓄养新奴婢者，将被处以300元以下的罚款，并强制释放其奴婢。
7. 所有区县政府和公安局应在三个月内向省政府报告禁令执行结果，这些报告由省政府转送内政部审议。
8. 上述措施自公布之日起生效。
